    Pretorsion theories with a fixed component #

    • (T, mod) and (mod, F) are pretorsion theories for every quotient-closed T and subobject-closed F (Section 3, before Lemma 3.1).
    • Proposition 3.2. For a fixed quotient-closed T, the second components F with (T, F) a pretorsion theory are closed under arbitrary intersections (isPretorsionTheory_iInf). The finite case (isPretorsionTheory_inf) is proved by induction on length, dividing by one reject at a time with IsShortPreexact.of_quotient; this replaces Lemma 3.1 and the transport (3.1) of the manuscript. The arbitrary case chooses, for each object, a finite subfamily with maximal reject.
    • Lemma 3.3 (isPretorsionTheory_of_reject_trace), Lemma 3.4 (prop_of_prop_cokernel_reject) and Proposition 3.5 (isPretorsionTheory_iInf_left), the last two via the realization criterion (Lemma 3.7).

    The inductive step of Proposition 3.2: if (T, F) satisfies (2.4) at X, G ⊆ F is subobject-closed and (T, G) satisfies (2.4) at X / r_F(X), then (T, G) satisfies (2.4) at X.

      Lemma 3.4. Let (T, F) be a pretorsion theory and G ⊇ F subobject-closed. If X / r_G(X) ∈ T, then X ∈ T.
